name: Guni
overview: Guni is a male figure from the tribe of Naphtali, identified specifically as a son of Naphtali. He is mentioned among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, indicating his place within the early Israelite family history. Additionally, his descendants, known as the Gunites, are noted in the census records of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Guni is a proper name meaning 'spotted sand grouse.' This name is recorded in the Scriptures without indication of divine naming or special title, simply serving as an identifier within the genealogy.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Guni as a son of Naphtali. Beyond this, no other family relationships are detailed in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Guni's significance lies primarily in his role as a progenitor within the tribe of Naphtali, contributing to the lineage of Israel during the patriarchal period. His inclusion among those who went to Egypt highlights the continuity of God's covenant people through a critical phase of their history. The mention of the Gunites in the census further affirms the ongoing legacy of his descendants within the nation of Israel.
